reasoning_content:
The volume `nebu_minio_data` still exists — `docker volume rm` probably failed. It's because the container was still attached and restarting. The volume is empty (minio failed at the tmp directory rename, so no data was written). But the ownership inside the volume is still root-owned — wait, the volume is empty, so when it gets freshly mounted, the contents of the image's /data should be copied in (docker copies the image's directory contents into an empty volume). The problem: I deleted the old volume, but then `docker volume rm` errored out (set -e interrupted the script after the build — no wait, the build succeeded, and then the rm failed, so set -e made the whole thing exit 1). The minio container is still using the old image (a3c826) and the old volume.

To do: 1) stop and delete the minio container, 2) delete the volume, 3) docker compose up -d again (compose will detect the image change and recreate the container).
